NutriCorp Foods - Q3 2023 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the NutriCorp Foods Q3 2023 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. During the Q&A session, please press star then one on your touchtone phone if using a landline or the raise hand icon if using the webcast. To withdraw your question, press star then two. Today's conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NutriCorp Foods' Q3 2023 results. Joining me on the call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer; Taylor Kim, Chief Growth Officer; and Morgan Patel, Chief Supply Chain Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from these statements.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera (CEO):
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report our results for Q3 2023. We delivered strong performance despite ongoing macroeconomic headwinds and inflationary pressures.

Today, I'll be focusing on seven key areas: key achievements and challenges in the quarter, market share trends for major brands, EPS guidance and key assumptions, performance of key brands and product categories, volume and price/mix analysis, discussion of pricing actions and revenue growth management strategies, and overall company performance highlights.

First, regarding key achievements and challenges in the quarter. We delivered a resilient quarter amid a volatile macro environment in the Food & Beverage sector, where input cost inflation and shifting consumer preferences continue to test the industry. Net sales grew 7.2% year-over-year to $1.18 billion, marking our third consecutive quarter of organic growth. This was driven by a healthy mix of volume expansion and pricing actions. Volume grew 4.1% globally, with particular strength in our Beverages segment, up 6.8% on the back of robust demand for functional beverages. Our VitaBoost line of plant-based protein shakes saw 22% volume growth, capturing share in the $15 billion U.S. RTD protein market, where we're now the number three player behind market leaders like Premier Protein and Core Nutritionals. This aligns with the broader trend of premiumization, with consumers trading up to health-focused SKUs with 10-15% higher price points.

Gross margins expanded 210 basis points to 38.4%, our strongest in two years. This was fueled by targeted supply chain initiatives, including a 15% reduction in logistics costs through our new AI-optimized routing platform, partnered with FourKites, which improved on-time delivery to 98%. We also executed SKU rationalization across our Snacks portfolio, pruning 12% of low-velocity items like underperforming legacy chips, which boosted inventory turns from 8.2x to 9.5x and freed up $45 million in working capital.

Regionally, North America was our powerhouse, delivering 9.5% sales growth to $720 million, powered by e-commerce acceleration. Our DTC platform hit $150 million in run-rate sales, up 35% year-over-year, as we leaned into Amazon and Instacart partnerships, achieving 25% ACV penetration in key metros like Chicago and Atlanta. In EMEA, sales rose 5.2% to $280 million, with standout performance in plant-based dairy alternatives. Our GreenSip almond milks gained 3 points of market share in the UK, per Nielsen data, amid the EU's push for sustainable labeling under the Green Deal.

On the strategic front, we hit key milestones in sustainability and innovation. Our Zero Waste by 2028 initiative diverted 75% of manufacturing waste from landfills, earning us a spot on the Dow Jones Sustainability Index for F&B. R&D investments yielded two new launches: a stevia-sweetened energy drink line with 50% less sugar, targeting Gen Z's wellness wave, and a cocoa-free chocolate snack using upcycled jackfruit, addressing the 25% year-over-year spike in cocoa prices that plagued peers like Hershey and Mondelez.

Adjusted EBITDA came in at $185 million, up 12% year-over-year, with margins at 15.7%, a testament to our disciplined SG&A control, holding flat at 18% of sales despite $10 million in wage inflation offsets through productivity gains.

That said, we weren't immune to industry headwinds. Commodity inflation eroded 150 basis points of gross margin potential, with sugar up 18% and edible oils up 12% year-over-year, per Bloomberg data. In our Snacks segment, this pressured volumes down 1.2% as we lapped aggressive pricing from last year, though we mitigated via futures hedging covering 70% of Q4 needs.

APAC remained a soft spot, with sales flat at $120 million due to China's economic slowdown and post-COVID inventory destocking at key retailers like Carrefour Asia. Velocity in our ready-to-drink teas dropped 8% in Southeast Asia, where health-conscious consumers shifted to local kombucha brands amid rising disposable income pressures.

Supply chain disruptions lingered, particularly in LATAM, where Brazil's coffee export delays, exacerbated by El Niño weather patterns, hiked roast-and-ground costs 22%. This hit our BrewMaster instant coffee line, contributing to a 3% regional sales dip to $60 million.

Consumer trends posed another hurdle: the health halo shift away from indulgent snacks. IRI data shows a 5% category contraction in savory snacks, and while we gained share through reformulations, it required $8 million in incremental marketing to maintain household penetration at 42%.

Operationally, our ERP migration to SAP S/4HANA, now 60% complete, incurred $12 million in one-time costs, temporarily lifting CapEx to 4.2% of sales. We're on track for full go-live by Q1 2024, which will unlock $20 million in annual procurement savings.

Looking ahead, we're positioning NutriCorp for accelerated growth in a $4.5 trillion global F&B market projected to grow at 5.2% CAGR through 2028, per Statista. Key levers include doubling R&D spend to 2.5% of sales for next-gen precision fermentation proteins, akin to Perfect Day's dairy tech. We're also expanding omnichannel with 500 new C-store doors via our PepsiCo distribution alliance and piloting blockchain traceability for 80% of our supply chain to meet retailer demands like Walmart's Project Gigaton.

Second, concerning market share trends for major brands. Drawing from the latest IRI and Nielsen syndicated data through the most recent 12-week period ending October 8th, NutriCorp continues to outperform the broader Food & Beverage category, expanding our total market share to 14.2% across our core segments, up 110 basis points year-over-year. This marks our 11th consecutive quarter of share gains, driven by a combination of volume-led growth, strategic pricing discipline, and accelerated innovation in high-velocity channels like convenience and e-commerce.

Let me break this down by our key brand franchises, starting with beverages, which represent 65% of our portfolio.

In carbonated soft drinks, a $85 billion global category still growing at low-single digits amid the shift to healthier alternatives, Zest Cola has solidified its position as the number two brand behind Coca-Cola's Coke Classic. We've gained 1.8 percentage points to reach 27.4% U.S. market share, per Nielsen, fueled by a 4.2% volume increase versus the category's flat performance. Key drivers include our Zest Zero Revolution reformulation, which cut sugar by 40% using stevia and monk fruit blends, boosting trial rates by 15% in IRI household scanner data. Distribution expanded to 92% ACV nationally, with particular strength in the Southeast where we hit 98% ACV through enhanced Kroger and Publix shelf sets.

Regionally, North America remains our powerhouse, but we're making inroads in EMEA. In the UK, Zest gained 2.1 points to 19% share, outpacing PepsiCo's portfolio amid our Tesco exclusive Zest Lite multipack launch. APAC is a bright spot too—India saw a 3.5-point jump to 12% share via localized mango and guava flavors, leveraging our new $150 million bottling facility in Gujarat to improve out-of-stock rates from 18% to 4%.

Strategically, we're countering private label erosion—now at 22% category share—through premiumization. Our Zest Reserve line, with natural colors and flavors, commands a 25% price premium and grew 28% year-over-year, capturing share from mid-tier players like Dr Pepper Snapple.

Turning to energy drinks, a $52 billion category exploding at 8% CAGR globally, Surge Energy extended its lead as the number three brand behind Monster and Red Bull, hitting 18.6% U.S. share—up 2.4 points. This reflects 7% volume growth, double the category rate, powered by our nootropic-infused Surge Focus variant, which resonated with Gen Z via TikTok-driven campaigns generating 500 million impressions.

Velocity metrics are stellar: Surge's equivalent base volume per store surged 12%, driven by cooler door expansions to 75% C-store ACV. In LATAM, Brazil delivered a standout 4.2-point gain to 15% share, where our partnership with Ambev enhanced cold-space dominance in over 50,000 independents. Challenges persist in Western Europe, where regulatory scrutiny on caffeine caps shaved 0.5 points, but our compliant Surge Hydrate with electrolytes and B-vitamins mitigated this, growing 35% and stealing share from niche players like Celsius.

Our technical playbook here includes AI-optimized supply chain forecasting via our SAP S/4HANA implementation, reducing stockouts by 22% and enabling just-in-time production of low-cal variants at our Ohio facility.

In non-alcoholic beverages, encompassing sparkling waters and functionals, a $120 billion category with 5% growth, PureSpring maintained its number one position at 32% U.S. share, flat year-over-year but defending against premium insurgents like LaCroix and Bubly. Volume held steady at +1%, with share stability masking underlying strength: our PureSpring Infusions line grew 22%, gaining 1.5 points in flavored seltzers.

Regionally, APAC is transformative—China's market share doubled to 8% via e-commerce tie-ups with Tmall, where functional immunity drinks tapped post-COVID demand. In North America, we're addressing health halo erosion from plant-based milks by launching PureSpring Plant-powered almond-kefir hybrids, projected to add 0.8 points in FY24.

Shifting to snacks, our $40 billion adjacency growing at 6%, CrunchBar chocolate-coated bars expanded to 11.2% share, +1.1 points, outrunning Hershey and Mars via 9% volume gains. This stems from our high-protein reformulation, 15g per bar, aligning with the 25% year-over-year surge in protein snacking occasions per SPINS data.

NutriBites savory nuts gained 0.9 points to 9.8% share, dominating dollar sales growth at +14% versus category +4%. In EMEA, Germany saw 2.3-point expansion to 14% through Rewe hypermarket resets, emphasizing our sustainable sourcing story—100% Rainforest Alliance nuts.

Across brands, we're navigating macro headwinds like 3-5% inflation in commodities, sugar up 12%, aluminum +8%, with VMS pricing up 4.2% while preserving margins at 28.5%. Share gains are amplified by channel shifts: e-commerce now 18% of sales, up from 12%, where our DTC platform drove 45% growth; and convenience, at 25% of volume with 6% share expansion.

Technically, our $300 million BevCore 2.0 initiative—encompassing precision fermentation for natural sweeteners and blockchain traceability—positions us for regulatory tailwinds like the EU's Green Deal. Competitively, we're chipping away at PepsiCo's 22% beverage share and Monster's energy fortress through M&A tuck-ins, like our recent $200 million acquisition of a functional RTD coffee brand.

Looking ahead, we expect full-year share expansion of 80-100 basis points, with Q4 acceleration from holiday multipacks and limited editions. Risks include private label velocity in discounters like Aldi and Lidl at 28% snack share and FX volatility in emerging markets, but our hedge book covers 85% exposure.

Third, in terms of EPS guidance and key assumptions. We're guiding to adjusted diluted EPS of $2.85 to $3.00 for the full year, representing 14% to 20% growth over our prior year adjusted EPS of $2.50. This puts us on track for our mid-teens compound annual growth rate through the cycle, even as we navigate a dynamic macro environment in the Food & Beverage space.

Let me break this down by the major drivers, starting with the top line. We're assuming organic net revenue growth of 5% to 7% for the full year, building on the 6.2% organic growth we delivered in Q3. This reflects a balanced mix: pricing actions of 3% to 4%, with volumes flat to up 2%. Pricing remains disciplined—think targeted increases on core categories like our Zest Cola beverages and NutriBites protein bars, where we've seen elasticities hold steady at around -1.5 to -2.0, similar to what we've observed across peers like PepsiCo and Keurig Dr Pepper. Volume growth will be anchored by our healthier SKUs; plant-based dairy alternatives, now 15% of our Refrigerated portfolio, grew 12% year-over-year in Q3, outpacing the category average per Nielsen data.

Regionally, North America—about 55% of our revenue—should deliver 6% to 8% organic growth, fueled by share gains in the convenience channel. We're gaining 110 basis points in energy drinks versus Monster and Red Bull, thanks to our Surge Energy line with zero-sugar formulations hitting 25% distribution at Circle K and 7-Eleven. EMEA, at 25% of sales, is a tougher story: we're guiding 2% to 4% growth here, pressured by softer consumer sentiment and regulatory headwinds like the UK's HFSS restrictions on high-fat, sugar, salt products. That said, our reformulated GreenSip yogurts, now under 5g sugar per serving, are mitigating this with 8% volume uplift. Asia-Pacific rounds it out at 20% of revenue, where we're expecting 8% to 10% growth—double-digit in India and Southeast Asia from e-commerce penetration, now 12% of APAC sales via platforms like Shopee and Flipkart, and new premium RTD coffee launches competing head-on with Nestlé's Nescafé ecosystem.

Gross margins are a highlight: we expect 150 to 200 basis points of expansion to 38.5% to 39.0%, up from 37.1% last year. This is driven by productivity savings of $180 million from our LeanNutriCorp initiative—automation of three bottling lines in Mexico and Ohio, yielding 15% throughput gains—and supply chain optimizations via our SAP S/4HANA ERP rollout, now live in 80% of plants. Input costs are the wildcard: we're baking in 2% to 3% inflation, down from 5% last year, with cocoa stabilizing post the 2024 Ivory Coast shortages, we've locked in 70% of needs at $4,200 per ton via forward contracts, dairy flat on ample Midwest supply, and PET resin easing 10% on lower oil. We'll proactively manage any wheat volatility from Black Sea disruptions through our Midwest grain hedges.

On the bottom line, adjusted operating expenses should run flat as a percentage of sales at 22.5%, with marketing up modestly to 8.5% of revenue to support velocity on innovation launches—like our AI-optimized flavor profiling for the upcoming ZeroWave electrolyte drinks. SG&A leverage comes from zero-based budgeting, targeting $50 million in overhead cuts. Interest expense is projected at $120 million, reflecting our $1.2 billion term loan at SOFR+175bps, with $300 million in debt paydown from strong free cash flow—expected at $850 million, or 105% FCF conversion. Our effective tax rate holds at 23.5%, assuming no material changes to OECD Pillar Two rules impacting our EU ops.

Capex guidance is $550 million, or 6.8% of sales—skewed to high-ROI projects like a $150 million aseptic filling line in Vietnam for ambient plant milks and precision agriculture tech with John Deere for our U.S. orchard network, aiming to cut water usage 20%. Share repurchases remain opportunistic at $400 million under our $1.5 billion authorization, prioritizing EPS accretion above 8% IRR.

Strategically, this guidance embeds our HealthForward 2025 playbook: 20% of RTD portfolio innovation spend on functional beverages—probiotics, adaptogens—targeting the $50 billion global wellness drink market growing at 9% CAGR per Euromonitor. We're also de-risking via supply chain diversification, with 40% of cocoa now from West Africa alternatives and Brazil, and hedging 60% of FX exposure, USD strength a $20 million tailwind. Risks include potential escalation in U.S.-China tariffs hitting our APAC imports or prolonged inflation eroding at-home consumption versus away-from-home recovery.

Fourth, looking at performance of key brands and product categories. We're thrilled with our resilient performance amid a dynamic macroeconomic environment, where input cost inflation for key commodities like sugar, cocoa, and dairy proteins has pressured margins across the industry. Consolidated net revenues reached $2.48 billion, up 8% as reported and 6% on an organic basis, excluding FX headwinds and the impact from last year's divestiture of our non-core European confectionery unit.

Organic revenue growth was propelled by a healthy mix of 2% volume growth, 2% pricing actions, and a robust 1% net price realization from favorable mix shifts toward premium and health-oriented SKUs. This marks our 11th consecutive quarter of positive organic growth, outpacing the global Food & Beverage category average of 3%, per Nielsen data. Market share gains totaled 110 basis points year-over-year across our core markets, fueled by targeted innovation and distribution expansion.

Our Beverages segment delivered standout results, with organic revenues up 9%, representing 55% of segment growth from volume and the balance from pricing and premiumization. Carbonated soft drinks, our largest subcategory at 45% of Beverages, grew 6% organically to contribute strongly. Our flagship Zest Cola—the number two CSD in North America behind only Coca-Cola—posted 8% volume growth, gaining 80 basis points of market share to 18.5%, driven by our Zest Zero Sugar reformulation with stevia and monk fruit, which captured 25% of Zest's total volume amid the low/no-sugar trend. In EMEA, Zest expanded into 5,000 new points of distribution in the UK and Germany, offsetting softer on-premise recovery post-COVID.

Non-carbonated beverages were the star, surging 14% organically. PureSpring, our juice and plant-based smoothie line, achieved 20% growth, fueled by the launch of three new organic cold-pressed variants, including a turmeric-ginger immunity booster that resonated strongly in APAC, where revenues jumped 25% on e-commerce platforms like Tmall and Shopee. Energy drinks under Surge Energy grew 12%, gaining share in LATAM against Red Bull through our Surge Zero low-cal option and soccer sponsorships with Liga MX teams. Regionally, North America led with 11% growth, while APAC faced headwinds from China's lockdowns, limiting us to 7% growth there.

Snacks & Convenience delivered steady 4% organic growth, with resilience against private label pressure. Savory snacks, led by CrunchBar—our kettle chip and popcorn portfolio—grew 5%, capturing 90 basis points of ACV share in the U.S. to 22%, per IRI data. This was underpinned by our Better-for-You initiative, introducing air-fried, 40% less sodium SKUs that drove 15% category penetration. Sweet snacks softened 2% due to elevated cocoa costs up 30% year-over-year; our NutriBites brand mitigated this with 10% growth via protein-fortified, high-fiber bars positioned against KIND and RXBAR, emphasizing clean-label credentials.

Convenience foods rounded out the segment with 6% growth, led by ReadyEats meal kits and frozen appetizers. Premiumization—higher-margin organic and plant-based options—contributed 3 points of growth. In North America, we gained 120 basis points share versus Conagra's lines through partnerships with Uber Eats for heat-and-eat bundles.

Our Nutrition & Dairy segment grew 8% organically, outpacing peers like Danone and Chobani. Yogurt and fermented dairy expanded 10%, with our ProBio Greek Yogurt line—now with 25g protein per serving—driving 18% volume uplift and 150 basis points market share gain in the U.S. to 14%. Plant-based alternatives under GreenSip exploded 25%, riding the 15% category growth per Euromonitor, with new barista blends capturing café channels in EMEA.

North America, 55% of revenues, saw 8% organic growth, led by channel shifts to club and e-commerce, up 22% year-over-year, with health trends boosting premium SKUs to 35% of sales mix. EMEA grew 4% despite 5% inflation drag; UK volume dipped 1% from excise taxes on sugary drinks, but Germany offset with 12% premium dairy gains. APAC grew 6%, tempered by China volumes down 3%; India shone with 18% Zest expansion via rural kirana stores. LATAM was resilient at 7% growth, with Brazil's energy drinks up 15% amid economic recovery.

Looking ahead, we're doubling down on health & wellness, targeting 50% of portfolio low-sugar/no-added-sugar by FY25, sustainability with 100% recyclable packaging for Zest by Q4 2024, reducing Scope 3 emissions 20% via regenerative agriculture for cocoa and nuts, and digital transformation. We've invested $150 million in our AI-driven demand sensing platform, improving forecast accuracy to 92% and cutting inventory waste 15%. R&D spend rose 12% to $250 million, yielding 45 new SKUs, including upcycled ingredient snacks from potato peels.

Competitively, IRI data shows us leading CSD volume growth versus PepsiCo and Keurig Dr Pepper, while in yogurt, we're number three in the U.S. premium segment. Risks remain—commodity volatility and potential U.S. recession could pressure volumes—but our gross margin expansion initiative via precision fermentation and supply chain hedging positions us well.

Fifth, reviewing volume and price/mix analysis. We delivered reported net revenues of $2.48 billion, up 8.2% year-over-year, and organic net revenue growth of 7.2%. This marks our sixth consecutive quarter of positive organic growth amid persistent food-away-from-home inflation averaging 4.8% globally and softening consumer sentiment in key developed markets.

Organic net revenue growth broke down to +0.8% volume growth and a robust +6.4% price/mix contribution. This balance underscores our disciplined execution on pricing strategies while protecting—and in many cases growing—our market share through innovation and targeted portfolio actions. For context, this compares favorably to industry peers: while Coca-Cola reported organic revenue growth of 6% with similar price/mix tailwinds, our snack segment outperformed PepsiCo's Frito-Lay North America volumes by 200 basis points.

Volume growth of +0.8% was a sequential improvement from Q2, reflecting stabilization in consumer demand as pantry-loading trends normalized. We gained 40 basis points of market share globally, per Nielsen and IRI data, driven by our HealthForward initiative—a $250 million investment in low- and no-sugar formulations.

Segmentally, Beverages volumes declined -1.2%, pressured by a 3% category contraction in CSDs due to health shifts. However, we offset this with +5.2% volume growth in emerging RTD coffee and tea platforms, like our AquaBrew iced lattes, which captured 12% market share in the $15 billion U.S. RTD coffee segment, outpacing Starbucks' packaged growth. Plant-based alternatives like OatSplash milk grew volumes +8%, aligning with a 15% category expansion.

Snacks saw a standout +4.5% volume growth, fueled by +7% in savory snacks like our rebranded ZestChips baked varieties, benefiting from air-fryer trend tie-ins and e-commerce penetration rising to 22% of sales. Premium nut mixes under NutriBites added +12% volumes, capitalizing on the $10 billion global healthy snacking boom.

Regionally, North America volumes grew +2.1%, with snacks leading at +5.3% on strong convenience store velocity, up 4% per Circana data, and beverages flat as we lapped tough prior-year CSD comparisons. EMEA was -0.5%, impacted by -2% volumes in beverages from regulatory sugar taxes in the UK and France, but mitigated by +3% in snacks via localized flavors like Harissa-spiced ZestChips in the Middle East. Latin America and Asia-Pacific aggregate +3.2%, with LATAM snacks +6% on economic recovery in Brazil and Mexico, and APAC beverages +4% driven by +15% volumes in sparkling waters amid China's zero-alcohol youth trend.

Turning to price/mix, up 6.4%—our strongest driver and a testament to our Value Discipline Framework, which uses AI-powered dynamic pricing models analyzing 50+ inputs like commodity costs, cocoa up 25% year-over-year, elasticities, and competitor actions. This exceeded our guided 5-6% range, reflecting +4.2% pricing actions, weighted toward everyday low-price SKUs to protect volume. In snacks, we implemented 7-9% list price hikes on 60% of the portfolio, passing through 80% of wheat and palm oil inflation. Mix shift +2.2%, propelled by premiumization. Beverages saw a 300 basis point shift to higher-margin RTDs and functional waters like VitaminInfuse, with 25% gross margins versus 15% for legacy CSDs. Snacks benefited from +5% mix in protein-enriched bars.

Strategically, we're leaning into portfolio reshaping: divesting $100 million in low-margin legacy CSDs to fund $400 million in innovation, targeting 10% of revenues from super-premium by FY25—like collagen-infused sparkling juices competing with Olipop's 50% growth. We've rolled out SmartShelf AI in 5,000 North American stores for real-time assortment optimization, boosting price/mix by 1.5 points via personalized bundling, snack-beverage packs up 20% velocity. In EMEA, eco-friendly packaging on 40% of snacks justified +2% premium pricing, resonating with 65% of Gen Z consumers per our Kantar surveys.

Looking ahead, we expect Q4 organic growth of 6-7%, with volume +1-2% as RTD momentum builds and price/mix 5-6% amid moderating inflation, global food CPI now +3.2%. Risks include potential elasticity pushback in APAC if rice costs spike further, but our 65% fixed-price commodity hedges position us well.

Sixth, analyzing discussion of pricing actions and revenue growth management strategies. Our pricing actions and broader revenue growth management—or RGM—strategies were pivotal in delivering our 7.2% organic net revenue growth this quarter, outpacing the industry average of 4.1% as reported by NielsenIQ. This marks our fifth consecutive quarter of positive organic growth amid persistent inflationary headwinds, supply chain volatility from Red Sea disruptions, and softening consumer demand in core categories like carbonated soft drinks and savory snacks.

Our net revenue realization reached 5.8% in Q3, up from prior quarters and well ahead of our long-term target of 4-5%. This was driven by a targeted list price architecture across our portfolio, with gross pricing up 7.1% offset partially by elevated trade spend at 1.3% of net revenue—a 20 basis points improvement year-over-year due to optimized promotional ROI.

In Beverages, 42% of our revenue, we implemented 6-8% list price increases on high-velocity SKUs like Zest Cola and Surge Energy drinks, citing cocoa and aluminum cost escalations up 15% and 12% year-over-year, respectively. This yielded a 6.2% NRR, helping us maintain share versus PepsiCo's Gatorade line in sports hydration.

In Snacks & Convenience Foods, 38% of revenue, we took measured 4-6% hikes on premium items like Harvest Nut bars and ZestChip kettle chips, focusing on premiumization to counter private label pressure from Aldi and Lidl. Gross margins expanded 210 basis points to 38.4%, echoing Mondelez's playbook on everyday low pricing for core lines while protecting ASPs on health-focused extensions.

Dairy & Plant-Based, 20% of revenue, saw pricing flattish at +2.1% NRR, reflecting competitive intensity from Oatly and Chobani in alt-milks. We leaned into value engineering, reformulating PlantPure yogurt to reduce sugar by 15% without price erosion, boosting household penetration by 3.2%.

Importantly, these actions were data-led. Our AI-powered pricing engine, built on partnership with PROS and integrated with IRI and Circana panels, simulated over 1.2 million price elasticity scenarios quarterly. This allowed dynamic adjustments—e.g., micro-pricing on e-commerce platforms like Amazon, where we captured 2.5x the basket uplift versus brick-and-mortar.

Pricing wasn't a lone driver; volume grew 0.8%, with mix adding 0.6% through portfolio optimization. We saw velocity gains in better-for-you segments—up 4.1% in low-sugar beverages and 5.7% in protein snacks—driven by shopper migration toward health claims amid GLP-1 drug trends like Ozempic.

Key RGM levers included promotion optimization: reduced A&P inefficiency from 18% to 15% of revenue via machine learning models forecasting trade promotion uplift. Our PromoMax tool cut ineffective BOGO events by 25%, reallocating to high-ROI funded sampling, mirroring Coca-Cola's Fairlife strategy. SKU rationalization: exited 12% of low-velocity SKUs like legacy sugary cereals, pruning our portfolio from 2,800 to 2,450 active items. This boosted distribution efficiency and mix by 1.2%, with premium SKUs now 28% of sales, up from 22% year-over-year. Innovation pipeline: launched 14 new products, including a zero-sugar RTD coffee line partnering with Keurig Dr Pepper tech, contributing 1.9% to growth. Consumer testing via Kantar showed 85% repeat intent.

North America, 65% of revenue, had NRR of 6.4% amid 3% category deflation in salty snacks. We gained 1.2 share points in club channels via EDLP on bulk packs, offsetting Walmart's aggression. Europe, 18%, was more challenged at 4.2% NRR due to regulatory sugar taxes. Focused on volume recovery through multipacks, holding share versus Unilever's ice cream. Emerging Markets, 17%, star performer with 8.7% NRR and 5.2% volume, fueled by urbanization in India and Brazil. Local production in Pune ramped 20%, mitigating FX headwinds.

Our RGM framework is anchored in consumer-centric pricing, elasticity-led with 92% actions within 1% of optimal, channel excellence with omnichannel pricing parity, growing D2C to 8% of sales, and sustainability-linked premiums—e.g., 10% price premium on recyclable packaging lines, resonating with 67% of Gen Z shoppers per our NPS surveys.

Looking ahead, we expect Q4 NRR of 5.0-5.5%, with full-year organic growth of 6-7%. Risks include potential tariff escalations on imported flavors and palm oil volatility +22% forecast by Mintec. Mitigants: hedging 70% of 2025 input costs and accelerating right-sizing initiatives, targeting 150 basis points gross margin expansion.

Seventh, examining overall company performance highlights. These results underscore NutriCorp Foods' resilient execution amid a dynamic macroeconomic backdrop in the Food & Beverage sector. We're reporting another quarter of strong top-line growth, margin expansion, and disciplined cost management, positioning us well for FY24 acceleration.

Consolidated net revenues reached $2.48 billion, up 8.2% year-over-year, or 6.1% on an organic basis excluding FX and acquisitions. This marks our ninth straight quarter of organic growth, outpacing the global F&B industry's 3-4% average as reported by NielsenIQ. Adjusted EPS came in at $1.27, a robust 12.5% increase, driven by 210 basis points of gross margin expansion to 42.3% and operating income growth of 14%. EBITDA margins expanded 160 basis points to 22.8%, reflecting the benefits of our VITALS cost-savings program, which delivered $85 million in savings this quarter—on track for our $350 million annual target through supply chain digitization and zero-based budgeting.

Volume growth was solid at 3.8%, fueled by everyday low pricing strategies in core categories and premiumization in high-growth segments. Pricing actions contributed 4.5% to organic growth, moderating from prior quarters as input cost inflation eased to 2-3% for key commodities like sugar, cocoa, and edible oils—down from double digits last year, aligning with USDA and FAO forecasts. Free cash flow generation was exceptional at $450 million, up 25% year-over-year, supporting $200 million in share repurchases and a 10% dividend hike we announced pre-market.

Our Beverages division—55% of revenues—drove 9.5% organic growth to $1.36 billion. CSDs volumes grew 2%, with market share gains in the U.S. to 28.5% per IRI data, thanks to our HydraBoost zero-sugar line, which surged 22% amid consumer shifts toward low-cal options similar to PepsiCo's Zero Sugar momentum. Functional beverages, including probiotic VitaShots and electrolyte-enhanced PeakPulse, exploded 35%, capturing share in the $15 billion global RTD functional market projected by Euromonitor. Juices and waters were flat on volume but up 5% on pricing, bolstered by sustainable packaging initiatives like 100% rPET bottles, reducing virgin plastic by 25%.

Snacks & Confectionery, 30% of the portfolio, posted 7.2% organic growth to $745 million. Savory snacks volumes rose 5.1%, led by CrunchVita baked chip line, which gained 1.2 points of U.S. market share against Frito-Lay benchmarks, driven by air-fried formulations appealing to health-conscious Gen Z. Chocolate and confectionery faced 3% volume pressure from cocoa prices spiking 40% year-over-year—echoing Hershey's headwinds—but premium truffles and plant-based CocoGreen bars grew 18%, with margins holding at 38% via forward hedging. We're mitigating cocoa volatility through new West African sustainable sourcing partnerships, targeting 50% certified cocoa by FY25.

Our Nutrition & Dairy segment, 15% of revenues, had 4.8% organic growth to $375 million. Plant-based dairy alternatives like NutriMilq oat and almond milks volumes jumped 28%, riding the 12% category CAGR per SPINS data, grabbing share from Danone's Silk in North America. Yogurt and ready-to-drink nutritionals grew 6%, supported by e-commerce penetration now at 18% of segment sales.

North America delivered 9.8% organic growth, 65% of total revenues, with market share up 80 basis points to 24.2% across IRI tracked channels. Brick-and-mortar recovery post-COVID, plus omnichannel strength—Amazon and Walmart+ now 15% of U.S. sales—were key. EMEA grew 5.2% organically, tempered by UK's HFSS advertising restrictions, but offset by 12% growth in functional beverages in Germany and France. APAC was the star at 12.4% organic, led by 20% volume expansion in China via our new Shanghai plant and India distribution deals with Reliance Retail; capitalizing on urban millennials' premium snacking trends. Latin America grew 7%, with Brazil's CSDs up 15% on local pricing and soccer sponsorship tie-ins.

Strategically, these results reflect our Growth Accelerator 2025 playbook: portfolio premiumization now 42% of revenues, up from 35% in FY22, with high-single-digit returns on our $1.2 billion in tuck-in M&A like the recent GreenLeaf Juices acquisition. Technically, our AI-powered demand sensing platform—integrated with SAP IBP—improved forecast accuracy to 92%, cutting inventory by 18% and enabling just-in-time procurement amid Red Sea disruptions. Sustainability metrics on target: Scope 1&2 emissions down 22% year-over-year via regenerative agriculture with 200,000 acres committed, aligning with Nestlé's net-zero ambitions and boosting ESG appeal—our MSCI rating upgraded to 'A'.

Overall, we are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee to provide more detail on our financial results.

Jordan Lee (CFO):

We are managing our costs effectively and continue to invest in key growth initiatives.

Our balance sheet remains strong with $450 million in cash and marketable securities. We are committed to returning value to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

For the full year, we are raising our guidance for sales growth to 7-8% and adjusted EBITDA margins to 15.5%.
